title: Bundibugyo virus disease in outbreak settings: A practical clinical review

analysis.scope_and_question: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) is a severe filovirus infection caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an orthoebolavirus with diagnostic and countermeasure implications distinct from Ebola virus (EBOV).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has expanded substantially, with 7890 confirmed cases and 3799 deaths reported across 63 health zones in seven provinces as of 23 September 2026.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: BVD usually presents as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness; haemorrhagic manifestations are uncommon at presentation. No vaccine or specific therapeutic has established clinical efficacy against BDBV in humans; Ervebo is being evaluated within research protocols and the PARTNERS trial is evaluating MBP134 and remdesivir-based regimens.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Early outbreak investigation also showed that EBOV-oriented testing can fail to detect BDBV, making species-appropriate molecular testing essential when BDBV is epidemiologically plausible. Insecurity, displacement, laboratory and transport constraints, and delayed presentation continue to limit implementation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Supportive care remains the standard of management, but what can be delivered safely differs between peripheral facilities and dedicated filovirus treatment centres. First-contact facilities should prioritise recognition, separation, protected sampling, treatment of immediately life-threatening or common treatable conditions, and early referral; treatment centres can provide closer monitoring, advanced supportive care, and access to approved research protocols.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), a severe filovirus infection caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an orthoebolavirus distinct from Ebola virus (EBOV). It highlights the clinical presentation of BVD as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness, with rare haemorrhagic manifestations. The ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reported 7890 confirmed cases and 3799 deaths as of 23 September 2026. The review emphasizes the importance of species-appropriate molecular testing for BDBV, as EBOV-oriented tests may fail to detect it. It also outlines the limitations in outbreak management due to insecurity, displacement, and logistical challenges. Currently, no vaccine or specific therapeutic has established clinical efficacy against BDBV, with Ervebo and the PARTNERS trial evaluating potential treatments. The review underscores the need for tailored supportive care, with peripheral facilities focusing on immediate life-threatening conditions and early referral, while dedicated treatment centres provide advanced care and access to research protocols.

title: Characterizing population movement patterns during a Sudan Virus Disease outbreak to adjust response efforts, Uganda, 2022.

analysis.research_question_and_background: In September 2022, Uganda declared a Sudan virus disease outbreak in Mubende District, prompting the Ministry of Health to seek characterization of population movement patterns to identify high‐risk areas and guide response efforts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: From September to December 2022, response teams applied the Population Connectivity Across Borders (PopCAB) method, conducting focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and participatory mapping with case‐contacts and community members across three districts.
analysis.methods: The PopCAB approach involved purposive sampling of case‐contacts and community members, with data collected through structured focus groups, key informant interviews, and participatory mapping to capture local and cross‐border travel routes and motivations.
analysis.main_results: The analysis identified 69 locations across seven non‐contiguous districts, including healthcare facilities, gold mines, schools, and transportation hubs, and mapped local and cross‐border travel routes and reasons for travel.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that integrating community‐based mobility mapping into contact tracing enabled rapid identification of high‐risk areas beyond the outbreak epicenter, representing a novel application of PopCAB in an Ebola‐virus outbreak.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Ministry of Health teams used the PopCAB results to enhance surveillance, risk communication, and infection prevention at priority locations, leading to the detection of two cases in Kampala and 26 additional cases in newly targeted districts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report any limitations of the study.

analysis.summary_en: In September 2022 Uganda declared a Sudan virus disease outbreak in Mubende District, prompting the Ministry of Health to investigate population movement patterns to identify high‐risk areas. From September to December 2022, response teams used the PopCAB method, conducting focus groups, key informant interviews, and participatory mapping with case‐contacts and community members across three districts. The approach mapped 69 locations across seven districts, including healthcare facilities, gold mines, schools, and transport hubs, and identified local and cross‐border travel routes and motivations. Integrating community‐based mobility mapping into contact tracing enabled rapid identification of high‐risk areas beyond the epicenter, a novel application of PopCAB in an Ebola‐virus outbreak. The Ministry of Health applied these findings to enhance surveillance, risk communication, and infection prevention, detecting two cases in Kampala and 26 additional cases in newly targeted districts.

title: The welfare and productivity losses associated with the death of an index case of Ebola Bundibugyo Virus Disease reported in Kenya on 6 October 2026

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to estimate the welfare and productivity losses associated with the death of the index case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in Kenya, as EBVD was imported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo on 3 October 2026.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Kenya, focusing on the economic impact of the death of the index case of EBVD on 6 October 2026. It used a societal perspective to assess the losses.
analysis.methods: The study employed the human capital approach (HCA), willingness-to-pay small (WTP_S) and large (WTP_L) models, and willingness-to-accept small (WTA_S) and large (WTA_L) models to estimate the discounted welfare and productivity losses associated with the death of the index case of EBVD.
analysis.main_results: Under the HCA model, the death of the 40-year-old male patient is expected to result in a total welfare loss of Int$120,944 and a productivity loss of Int$40,763. Re-estimating the models with different discount rates and life expectancies showed variations in the estimated losses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the results as indicating that the death of the index case of EBVD would lead to significant welfare and productivity losses, highlighting the need for economic assessments in public health responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform Kenya’s Ministry of Health in advocating for increased investment in prevention, mitigation, and response to EBVD, particularly in areas such as International Health Regulations core capacities, universal health coverage, and WASH.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results were re-estimated under different assumptions, which may affect the robustness of the findings. The evidence is based on secondary sources and models, which may introduce uncertainty.

analysis.summary_en: This study estimates the welfare and productivity losses associated with the death of the index case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease (EBVD) in Kenya on 6 October 2026. The research was motivated by the importation of EBVD from the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the lack of economic evidence to guide public health investment. Using the human capital approach and various willingness-to-pay and willingness-to-accept models, the study found that the death of the 40-year-old male patient would result in a welfare loss of Int$120,944 and a productivity loss of Int$40,763 under the HCA model. Re-estimating the models with different discount rates and life expectancies showed variations in the estimated losses, with reductions under lower discount rates and increases under higher life expectancy assumptions. The authors concluded that the death of the index case would lead to significant economic losses, emphasizing the need for investment in public health infrastructure to mitigate the risk of EBVD becoming a national epidemic. title: Known pathogen, unprepared system: Bundibugyo virus and the diagnostic preparedness gap

analysis.research_question_and_background: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exposed a fundamental weakness in global diagnostic preparedness. Although BDBV had been recognized for nearly two decades and diagnostic tools existed, gaps across the diagnostic ecosystem delayed outbreak recognition and response.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a case study of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It examines the diagnostic preparedness gap through an analysis of the response to this outbreak.
analysis.methods: Diagnostic preparedness must shift toward adaptable syndromic and viral-family platforms, regional sequencing capacity, integrated surveillance systems, pre-positioned regulatory and validation pathways, resilient manufacturing, sustainable inter-epidemic financing, and clear global accountability.
analysis.main_results: The response to the BDBV outbreak should be understood not as an isolated diagnostic failure, but as a case study demonstrating why preparedness strategies built around individual pathogens are insufficient for future epidemic and pandemic threats.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: If the global community struggles to deploy diagnostics for a known pathogen, it is unlikely to respond effectively to a novel or highly divergent one.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The outbreak raises broader questions about the need for a more resilient and adaptable diagnostic ecosystem to address future epidemic and pandemic threats.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study, but the general implications suggest that the evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on a single case study.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the 2026 Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, highlighting a critical gap in global diagnostic preparedness. Despite BDBV being recognized for nearly two decades, the diagnostic ecosystem failed to translate existing technologies into timely public health action. The authors argue that the response to this outbreak should be viewed as a case study illustrating the inadequacy of pathogen-specific preparedness strategies for future threats. They propose a shift toward adaptable syndromic and viral-family platforms, regional sequencing capacity, and integrated surveillance systems. The study suggests that the global community may struggle to respond effectively to novel or highly divergent pathogens, emphasizing the need for a more resilient diagnostic ecosystem. While the findings are based on a single case study, they provide important insights into the limitations of current diagnostic preparedness and the importance of systemic improvements.

title: The Attenuation Paradox in Bundibugyo Virus Disease: Case Fatality, Ascertainment, and Delayed Outbreak Recognition

analysis.scope_and_question: Bundibugyo virus has caused three recognised outbreaks, and each was recognised late.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The usual reading of that record treats the delay as a failure of investment, diagnostics or governance. The evidence is organised around three comparison tables: the burden, severity and recognition interval of each outbreak; the presenting clinical features set against a matched Ebola virus series; and the point at which species assignment failed in each event.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: This review sets out a partly mechanistic alternative: the low case fatality ratio observed early in a Bundibugyo virus outbreak is itself one of the conditions that produces the delay, and the delay in turn depresses the observed ratio further. The 2026 epidemic, in which the confirmed ratio rose from 12.1% to 44.3% while the virus doubled every 5.5 days, fits this account better than it fits a change in virulence. The clinical syndrome does not discriminate between species: haemorrhage was documented in roughly a quarter of confirmed patients in both the 2007–08 Bundibugyo series and a 2014 Ebola virus series, so the presenting picture cannot carry the explanatory weight often placed on it.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The discriminating failures are instead genomic and diagnostic, and the early case fatality ratio operates as a surveillance trigger that is biased downward precisely when ascertainment is narrowest.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: A fatality ratio from the first weeks of a filovirus outbreak should therefore be read as an index of surveillance maturity rather than of danger, and escalation should be governed by species-inclusive confirmation.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the attenuation paradox in Bundibugyo virus disease, focusing on the delayed recognition of outbreaks and the low case fatality ratio observed early in these events. It challenges the conventional interpretation that delays are due to failures in investment, diagnostics, or governance, proposing instead that the low fatality ratio itself contributes to delayed outbreak recognition. The review presents evidence through three comparison tables, highlighting the lack of clinical discrimination between species and the role of genomic and diagnostic factors in shaping surveillance outcomes. The 2026 epidemic is cited as a case that aligns better with this explanation than with a change in virulence. The implications suggest that early fatality ratios should be interpreted as indicators of surveillance maturity rather than disease severity, emphasizing the need for species-inclusive confirmation in outbreak escalation decisions.

title: Live-cell diffracted X-ray blinking reveals Ebola virus VP40-driven budding dynamics and their regulation by cytoskeletal and lipid factors

analysis.research_question_and_background: Ebolavirus VP40 drives viral budding by remodeling the plasma membrane, yet the underlying real-time dynamics remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we applied Diffracted X-ray Blinking (DXB) to investigate how Ebolavirus VP40 affects membrane dynamics in living cells by monitoring millisecond-scale fluctuations in X-ray diffraction intensity.
analysis.methods: Expression of wild-type VP40 (wtVP40) from Zaire ebolavirus induced a progressive increase in membrane fluctuations, whereas the dimerization-defective mutant L117R and the oligomerization-deficient mutant I307R failed to enhance membrane motion despite comparable protein expression levels.
analysis.main_results: Consistent with these findings, only wtVP40 was efficiently released into the culture medium, indicating that increased membrane fluctuations correlate with budding competence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: DXB analysis further showed that wtVP40 increased the fast-moving population with higher decay constants, whereas the L117R and I307R mutants showed limited changes in the decay-constant distributions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Pharmacological perturbation studies demonstrated that VP40-induced membrane fluctuations are sensitive to both cytoskeletal integrity and phosphatidylserine availability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Expression of VP40 from Reston ebolavirus similarly enhanced membrane dynamics, suggesting that VP40-mediated membrane remodeling is conserved among Ebolaviruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the real-time dynamics of Ebolavirus VP40 in driving viral budding by using Diffracted X-ray Blinking (DXB) to monitor millisecond-scale membrane fluctuations in living cells. The research found that wild-type VP40 from Zaire ebolavirus significantly increased membrane motion, while dimerization and oligomerization-defective mutants did not, despite similar protein expression levels. These results were corroborated by the observation that only wild-type VP40 was efficiently released into the culture medium, indicating a correlation between membrane fluctuations and budding competence. DXB analysis revealed that wild-type VP40 increased the fast-moving population with higher decay constants, whereas the mutants showed minimal changes. The study also demonstrated that VP40-induced membrane fluctuations are influenced by cytoskeletal integrity and phosphatidylserine availability. The findings suggest that VP40-mediated membrane remodeling is conserved across Ebolaviruses, highlighting potential biophysical markers for viral assembly and antiviral strategies targeting budding. The evidence is strong, with clear results and implications for understanding viral mechanisms.

title: Measurement Error Correction and Multidimensional Aggregation in Epidemiological Surveillance Systems: Application to the Ebola Virus Disease Epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

analysis.research_question_and_background: Epidemiological surveillance systems produce decision-making indicators from data that may be affected by under-reporting, misclassification and notification delays. These errors can propagate through the extraction, transformation, loading and multidimensional aggregation stages.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This article proposes a mathematical framework that integrates measurement error correction into an ETL–data warehouse–OLAP decision architecture. The central problem is to determine whether the correction of a misclassification error can be performed before or after aggregation without changing the resulting indicator.
analysis.methods: A numerical instantiation based on a synthetic dataset calibrated on published parameters of the Ebola virus disease epidemic in North Kivu and Ituri (DRC, 2018–2020) illustrates this non-commutation and its consequences for the estimation of incidence and the reproduction number.
analysis.main_results: We show that the Rogan–Gladen estimator commutes with the roll-up operator only when the sensitivity and specificity parameters are homogeneous across the aggregated strata. A bias–variance analysis (Theorem 4) and a Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis (5,000 replicates, seven scenarios) further show that aggregate-level correction can have a slightly smaller variance but becomes biased when cases concentrate in poorly covered zones, and that the corrected indicators are highly sensitive to the assumed specificity when test positivity is close to the false-positive floor (a misspecification of 0.005 in specificity changes cumulative incidence by more than 100%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results lead to a design rule: when surveillance quality is heterogeneous, correction must be performed at the finest level at which the error parameters can be regarded as homogeneous, before any aggregation, because this is the only strategy that remains unbiased whatever the spatial distribution of cases.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The proposed framework thus provides a formal basis for designing surveillance decision-support systems that explicitly account for data quality.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: No individual-level surveillance data were used: the synthetic data are fully specified by a generation algorithm and a parameter table provided for reproducibility.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of measurement error in epidemiological surveillance systems, particularly in the context of Ebola virus disease. It presents a mathematical framework that integrates error correction into an ETL–data warehouse–OLAP architecture, aiming to improve the accuracy of decision-making indicators. The research demonstrates that the Rogan–Gladen estimator only commutes with the roll-up operator when sensitivity and specificity parameters are homogeneous across aggregated strata. A synthetic dataset based on the DRC Ebola epidemic illustrates the consequences of error correction at different stages. The authors conclude that correction should occur at the finest level where error parameters are homogeneous to ensure unbiased results. The study highlights the importance of accounting for data quality in surveillance systems and provides a formal basis for their design. However, the use of synthetic data limits the applicability of findings to real-world scenarios, and the framework's effectiveness depends on assumptions about test specificity.

title: Natural genus-exclusive four-position VP24 configuration in Bundibugyo virus links host interferon tone to a testable cell-type ordering

analysis.research_question_and_background: Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) causes outbreaks with lower case-fatality than Ebola virus (EBOV); its VP24 carries the only BDBV-specific functional difference mapped to date.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we integrate a sequence census, a human cell-type expression atlas, and a reanalysis of public infection data to connect the natural BDBV VP24 configuration to host interferon (IFN) tone and derive a testable cell-type ordering of post-entry IFN-mediated restriction.
analysis.methods: All 31 full-length BDBV VP24 records and all 36 complete 2026 outbreak genomes carried S83/Q135/H140/A141; none of the other five orthoebolavirus species assessed carried the complete set.
analysis.main_results: Two consensus-only single-position departures occurred among 860 callable copies in the surveillance data.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Δ, a baseline IFN-tone score, tracks the IFN-stimulated level attained by a cell and predicts the strength of IFN-mediated suppression of viral RNA accumulation in cells infected with BDBV carrying the VP24 defect: high Δ denotes stronger suppression, low Δ weaker.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Across 154 human cell types, Δ was higher in surface epithelia and circulating myeloid cells (enterocytes 1.28; monocytes 1.00) than in retinal and testicular cells (retinal pigment epithelium − 1.02; Sertoli cells − 0.68).
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A competing importin-α model predicted exemption in the 47 cell types with high Δ but low importin-α, including enteric epithelium and hepatocytes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the unique VP24 configuration in Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) and its association with host interferon (IFN) tone. The research aimed to connect the natural BDBV VP24 configuration to IFN-mediated restriction in different human cell types. By integrating a sequence census, a human cell-type expression atlas, and reanalysis of public infection data, the study identified that all 31 full-length BDBV VP24 records and 36 complete 2026 outbreak genomes carried the S83/Q135/H140/A141 configuration, which is absent in other orthoebolavirus species. The findings revealed that Δ, a baseline IFN-tone score, correlates with the strength of IFN-mediated suppression of viral RNA accumulation. The study also demonstrated that Δ was higher in surface epithelia and circulating myeloid cells compared to retinal and testicular cells. Additionally, a competing importin-α model predicted exemption in certain cell types with high Δ but low importin-α. These results provide insights into the cell-type-specific restriction of BDBV and highlight the importance of IFN tone in viral dynamics. However, the study's interpretation is limited by the reliance on a competing model and the absence of direct functional validation.

title: Doxycycline and Nitazoxanide as a Candidate Immunomodulatory Combination for the Early Management of Ebola Disease Caused by Bundibugyo Virus

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore potential immunomodulatory strategies for managing Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, given the high mortality rate and lack of approved treatments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where as of 5 November 2026, there were 10,741 confirmed cases and 5,230 deaths, with a significant proportion of deaths occurring in communities rather than treatment centers.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed pathology in Bundibugyo-infected macaques, identifying distinct immune profiles in fatal and survivor animals, and proposed a mechanism for doxycycline and nitazoxanide as an immunomodulatory combination.
analysis.main_results: Pathology in Bundibugyo-infected macaques showed that fatal cases had a myeloid hyperinflammatory profile with elevated interleukin-6 and myeloperoxidase, while survivors exhibited an intact T cell response.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as suggesting a potential immunomodulatory approach, proposing doxycycline and nitazoxanide as a combination targeting different immune pathways, based on the observed immune profiles.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of understanding immune dysregulation in Bundibugyo virus disease and suggest a promising avenue for early immunomodulatory interventions, which could be critical for managing outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not establish efficacy in Bundibugyo disease, as it is based on observations in macaques and lacks direct clinical evidence, which limits the strength of the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of doxycycline and nitazoxanide as an immunomodulatory combination for managing Bundibugyo virus disease. It highlights the high mortality rate and lack of approved treatments for this disease, emphasizing the need for alternative strategies. The research analyzed pathology in infected macaques, revealing distinct immune profiles in fatal and survivor cases. The authors propose that these drugs could target different immune arms, offering a mechanism for further testing. However, the study does not establish efficacy in Bundibugyo disease, underscoring the need for species-specific research. The findings suggest that focusing on immunomodulators may be a viable approach for addressing outbreaks, as these drugs are already available and inexpensive.

title: Cross-protective potential of Zaire ebolavirus-targeted vaccines against Bundibugyo virus: search strategies and review methods

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the cross-protective potential of Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV)-targeted vaccines against Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). It examines whether vaccines developed for EBOV can provide protection against BDBV, with an emphasis on human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses and Ebola virus disease. Reston and Bombali viruses are considered background or comparison entities unless human disease evidence is explicitly present.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic review with pre-specified search strategies, eligibility criteria, and core methodological components. It includes nine bibliographic databases (MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CENTRAL, CINAHL, Global Index Medicus, African Index Medicus, AJOL), full-text searching, dissertations, seven trial registries, six preprint servers, and regulatory and agency grey literature. The methods were deposited in accordance with PRISMA-S before any search was executed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review does not report any substantive conclusions or pooled estimates. It outlines the search strategies and methodological framework but does not provide results or interpretations related to the cross-protective potential of EBOV-targeted vaccines against BDBV.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report any controversies or evidence gaps. It does not address conflicting findings, unresolved mechanisms, or missing populations or regions. The evidence base is described but not analyzed for heterogeneity or gaps in the data.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review does not provide specific research or practice implications. It does not outline priorities for surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, vaccination, or policy. The implications section remains unaddressed in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This review outlines the methodology for a systematic analysis of the cross-protective potential of Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV)-targeted vaccines against Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). It specifies the search strategies, databases, and eligibility criteria used to identify relevant studies. However, it does not present any substantive results, conclusions, or implications. The review emphasizes the importance of systematic and transparent methods in evaluating vaccine efficacy across related viruses, but no findings are reported. The evidence base includes a range of sources, yet no analysis of the data is provided.

title: Beyond isolation: Clinical care as an outbreak control intervention for Ebola disease

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to challenge the conventional separation of outbreak control and clinical care in Ebola disease, highlighting the need to recognize clinical care as an integral part of outbreak management. The background emphasized that this separation may be administratively convenient but is epidemiologically misleading.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed the 2026 Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, focusing on the role of clinical care in outbreak dynamics. It considered the diverse pathways patients may take, including home, traditional healers, private clinics, and general healthcare facilities.
analysis.methods: The methods involved examining the interplay between clinical care quality, patient behavior, and transmission dynamics during the 2026 outbreak. It included reviewing experiences of care, communication, survival, and institutional behavior that shaped trust in treatment centers.
analysis.main_results: The results indicated that trust in Ebola treatment centers was influenced by the quality of care, communication, survival rates, and institutional behavior. Clinical quality was found to shape transmission by altering the timing and location of infectious contact.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that clinical care is not merely a humanitarian endpoint but an active intervention for outbreak control. This insight is novel in framing clinical care as a critical component of outbreak response strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of integrating clinical care into outbreak control efforts, emphasizing the need for accessible, trustworthy treatment facilities to encourage early patient presentation and reduce transmission risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on observational data and the absence of direct experimental evidence. However, the evidence is moderate in strength due to its focus on real-world outbreak dynamics and community behavior.

analysis.summary_en: This study challenges the traditional separation of clinical care and outbreak control in Ebola disease, arguing that clinical care is an active intervention for managing outbreaks. It analyzed the 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, highlighting how trust in treatment centers is shaped by care quality, communication, survival, and institutional behavior. The findings suggest that clinical care influences transmission dynamics by altering the timing and location of infectious contact. These insights have implications for improving outbreak response strategies by integrating clinical care into public health measures. The study's evidence is moderate in strength, as it is based on observational data rather than experimental methods. Limitations include the lack of direct experimental evidence and potential biases in community behavior reporting.

title: Recent Advances in Experimental Models to Study Endotheliopathy in Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers: Relevance to Lassa Virus

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on understanding the role of endothelial cells in the pathogenesis of viral hemorrhagic fevers (VHF), specifically examining whether endothelial infection drives the endotheliopathy underlying vascular leakage, coagulopathy, and inflammation in severe VHF. The central question is whether direct endothelial infection alone is sufficient to account for increased vascular permeability during Lassa fever, with a focus on Ebola viruses as the target entity.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of recent experimental advances in understanding endothelial involvement in VHF pathogenesis, with a focus on Ebola viruses and complementary evidence from other VHFs. It discusses experimental approaches such as endothelial cell infection in non-human primates and in vitro models, immune-endothelial crosstalk, and the effects of soluble or surface-exposed viral proteins on endothelial barrier integrity. The review does not report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that experimental evidence for LASV-induced endothelial cell activation and barrier dysfunction remains limited. However, it proposes that direct endothelial infection alone is insufficient to account for increased vascular permeability during Lassa fever. The findings are drawn from mechanistic insights from other VHFs, including the potential contributions of immune-endothelial interactions and soluble or surface-exposed viral proteins to vascular dysfunction.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that the mechanisms by which endothelial infection contributes to vascular leakage, coagulopathy, and inflammation in severe VHF remain unclear. It also notes that experimental evidence for LASV-induced endothelial cell activation and barrier dysfunction is limited, and there is a lack of standardized models for studying VHF-associated endotheliopathy.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for experimental and methodological priorities to improve the physiological relevance and standardization of models for studying VHF-associated endotheliopathy. It suggests the development of more advanced organ-on-chip and organoid technologies to better model the human vasculature and investigate barrier function in the context of VHFs, while considering biosafety constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of endothelial cells in the pathogenesis of viral hemorrhagic fevers (VHF), with a focus on Ebola viruses. It highlights the need for experimental models that capture the complexity of the vascular microenvironment to understand how endothelial infection contributes to vascular leakage, coagulopathy, and inflammation. The review notes that while experimental evidence for LASV-induced endothelial dysfunction is limited, immune-endothelial interactions and soluble viral proteins may play a significant role. It also discusses the potential of organ-on-chip and organoid technologies for modeling VHF-associated endotheliopathy and identifies methodological priorities for future research.

title: National Ebola preparedness policy architecture and health system readiness in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda: a scoping review anchored in the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak.

analysis.scope_and_question: This scoping review examines the national preparedness instruments and health system readiness of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda in the context of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak. The review focuses on the capacity of these countries to respond to the outbreak, including their surveillance systems, isolation capabilities, and provisions for managing displaced populations. The central question is how these countries' preparedness frameworks influenced the outbreak's trajectory.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework, Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews. National instruments in force at the outbreak's onset, International Health Regulations evaluations, and outbreak documents were sought from issuing bodies and charted against 52 component requirements across ten dimensions, with operational specificity as an eleventh.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review found that Uganda's national instruments addressed 47 of 52 components (90.4%), while the DRC's addressed 38 (73.1%). Uganda was rated higher in six dimensions, including surveillance, isolation capacity, displaced populations, and accountability, and equal in five. The DRC's response plan was highly specific in 21 of 37 provisions, indicating that its gap lay in standing arrangements rather than in response planning.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that both countries were inadequate in cross-border governance. Neither had a Bundibugyo-specific countermeasure provision. Additionally, the review notes that documentary analysis cannot establish causality between these differences and the varying outbreak courses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Priorities for research and practice include enhancing surveillance and isolation capacity in the DRC, improving cross-border governance in both countries, and developing national pathways for investigational Bundibugyo products.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review evaluates the national preparedness instruments and health system readiness of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak. The review maps the evidence against 52 component requirements across ten dimensions, with operational specificity as an eleventh. Uganda's instruments were more comprehensive, addressing 90.4% of the components, while the DRC's addressed 73.1%. Uganda was rated higher in six dimensions, including surveillance and accountability, and equal in five. The DRC's response plan was highly specific in 21 of 37 provisions, suggesting gaps in standing arrangements. Both countries lacked Bundibugyo-specific countermeasures and had inadequate cross-border governance. The review emphasizes the need for improved surveillance, isolation capacity, and cross-border coordination, as well as national pathways for investigational products.

title: Ebola Bundibugyo reaches Nigeria: implications for global travel, Hajj and Umrah.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the implications of an imported Bundibugyo virus case in Nigeria for global travel, Hajj and Umrah, emphasizing the need for rapid recognition, contact tracing, laboratory readiness, and cross-border coordination.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reports on an imported Bundibugyo virus case in Nigeria and examines the impact of Saudi Arabia’s Kenya-specific restrictions on travel measures and preparedness for Hajj and Umrah.
analysis.methods: The study relies on updated evidence regarding the Nigerian case and analyzes the travel restrictions implemented by Saudi Arabia in response to the Bundibugyo virus importation.
analysis.main_results: The evidence indicates no onward transmission of the Bundibugyo virus in Nigeria during the reported follow-up period, and Saudi Arabia’s restrictions highlight the balance between travel measures and preparedness for religious pilgrimages.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating the importance of maintaining vigilance and preparedness for global travel and religious events in the context of emerging viral threats, with no new causal mechanisms reported.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for enhanced surveillance and coordination across borders to manage the risk of viral importation and ensure preparedness for large gatherings such as Hajj and Umrah.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis, and the findings are supported by updated case reports and travel restrictions, providing moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the implications of an imported Bundibugyo virus case in Nigeria for global travel and religious pilgrimages like Hajj and Umrah. It highlights the necessity for rapid recognition, contact tracing, and cross-border coordination to prevent onward transmission. The research reports that no further transmission occurred in Nigeria during the follow-up period, while Saudi Arabia's travel restrictions underscore the balance between implementing proportionate measures and ensuring preparedness for large gatherings. The findings emphasize the importance of maintaining surveillance and readiness for viral threats, particularly in the context of international travel. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis, and the conclusions are supported by updated case reports and travel restrictions, offering moderate confidence in the interpretation.

title: Private healthcare facilities’ participation in Uganda’s viral hemorrhagic fever surveillance program: contributions, selective case capture, and underutilized early-warning potential

analysis.research_question_and_background: Private healthcare facilities are important initial points of contact, especially for patients with undifferentiated febrile illnesses in mixed health systems. However, their contribution to viral hemorrhagic fever surveillance remains to be quantified, particularly in outbreak-prone regions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of all suspected VHF specimen submissions recorded in Uganda’s national Result Dispatch System from 1 January 2023 to 14 August 2026, spanning the 2025 Sudan virus disease and 2026 Ebola (Bundibugyo virus, BDBV) outbreaks. Of 7,929 submissions, 504 (6.4%) were private.
analysis.methods: Ownership was classified against the national health facility master list. Pre-specified outcomes were test positivity, recorded bleeding, and alive-at-reporting status. Adjusted analyses used generalized linear mixed models with a district-level random intercept, pre-specified sensitivity analyses, and a test of effect modification by Kampala.
analysis.main_results: Private healthcare facilities contributed 21 of 149 VHF-positive submissions and 10 of 32 Ebola-positive submissions. During May–June 2026, they contributed 212 of 1,230 submissions and 10 of 20 Ebola-positive submissions; Ebola positivity was 4.72% versus 0.98% in public submissions (post-hoc comparison; crude odds ratio 4.99, p = 0.0007). Private ownership was associated with overall VHF positivity (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.44, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.95–6.05), recorded bleeding (4.97, 3.86–6.41), and alive-at-reporting status among known-status records (5.43, 4.09–7.21).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Private healthcare facilities contributed a small share of submissions but a disproportionate share of detections, recorded VHF-compatible bleeding far more often, and far more often reported patients still alive, unlike the post-mortem case-finding dominating public submissions in the capital.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support targeted, differentiated integration of private healthcare facilities into surveillance systems, highlighting their potential for early-warning and improved case detection in viral hemorrhagic fever outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Positivity attenuated after reporting-status adjustment (2.40, 1.34–4.28); intervals included 1 in alive-only and pre-2026 analyses. The evidence is moderate as it is based on retrospective data and requires prospective study to confirm effects on timeliness.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the role of private healthcare facilities in Uganda’s viral hemorrhagic fever surveillance system, particularly during outbreaks of Sudan virus disease and Ebola (Bundibugyo virus). It finds that while private facilities account for a small proportion of submissions, they contribute disproportionately to VHF-positive and Ebola-positive cases. Private ownership was associated with higher rates of recorded bleeding and alive-at-reporting status compared to public facilities. The study highlights the potential of private facilities for early-warning and improved case detection but emphasizes the need for prospective research to validate these findings. The evidence is moderate due to the retrospective nature of the analysis and the lack of direct causal conclusions.

title: Strengthening Disease Surveillance, Outbreak Preparedness, and Response Through Medical Laboratory Systems in Nigeria: Roles, Requirements, and Post-Ebola Reforms

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of medical laboratory systems in disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness, particularly in the context of Ebola viruses and related entities. The central question is how strengthening these systems can improve early detection and response to infectious disease threats, with a specific emphasis on Nigeria's experience post-Ebola.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative analysis of the role of medical laboratory systems in disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness, with an emphasis on the Ebola Virus Disease epidemic in West Africa and Nigeria's containment efforts. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that reliable laboratory systems are central to detecting infectious disease threats early and guiding a coordinated public health response required to sustain health security. It highlights the importance of rapid laboratory confirmation in containing outbreaks, as demonstrated by Nigeria's success in managing imported Ebola cases.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while the Ebola experience prompted major institutional and technical reforms, the evidence does not provide detailed information on the effectiveness of these reforms or their long-term impact on disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness. There is also a lack of specific data on the comparative performance of different laboratory systems.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for continued investment in strengthening medical laboratory systems to enhance disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness. It suggests that future research should focus on evaluating the effectiveness of these systems and addressing gaps in their implementation and performance.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the critical role of medical laboratory systems in disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness, particularly in the context of Ebola viruses and related entities. It highlights the 2014 Ebola Virus Disease epidemic in West Africa as a case study, showing how fragile diagnostic infrastructure can be, while Nigeria's successful containment of imported cases demonstrates the value of rapid laboratory confirmation. The review concludes that robust laboratory systems are essential for early detection and coordinated public health responses. It also identifies evidence gaps, such as the lack of detailed data on the effectiveness of reforms and comparative performance of different systems, and suggests future research priorities to address these gaps and improve health security.

title: Working harder, losing ground: surveillance under epidemic load in the first three months of the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak in the DR Congo, a retrospective analysis of situation reports

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how surveillance and diagnostic systems perform under increasing epidemic workload, particularly during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective longitudinal analysis was conducted using public DRC INSP situation reports and the INRB-UMIE BDBV2026-Data repository, covering 89 national reporting dates through 31 August 2026.
analysis.methods: The study used beta-binomial regression to model report-day proportions, negative-binomial regression for counts and laboratory throughput, and province-by-time interactions to assess strict positivity. Case/testing associations were based on true 24-hour intervals only.
analysis.main_results: Alert volume increased by 81% per 30 days (IRR 1.81, 95% CI 1.58–2.08), while alert-investigation coverage declined (OR 0.50, 0.34–0.73). Contact follow-up improved (OR 1.55, 1.37–1.76) and laboratory throughput increased (IRR 1.56, 1.41–1.73).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that surveillance and diagnostic activity scaled up, but alert-investigation coverage fell as workload increased, while contact follow-up improved. This highlights the complex relationship between testing volume and case reporting during an epidemic.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for adaptive surveillance strategies during outbreaks, emphasizing the importance of maintaining alert-investigation coverage despite rising workloads.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on situation reports and the potential for unequal reporting intervals to shape the administrative curve. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on retrospective analysis and does not account for real-time data.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the performance of surveillance and diagnostic systems during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It found that alert volume increased significantly, but alert-investigation coverage decreased as workload rose. Contact follow-up and laboratory throughput improved, but the relationship between testing volume and case counts was not independent. The study highlights the challenges of maintaining effective surveillance during epidemics and suggests the need for adaptive strategies. However, the findings are based on retrospective data and may be influenced by unequal reporting intervals, limiting their strength.

title: Development of Heterocyclic Small Molecule Antiviral Entry Inhibitors

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop novel antiviral therapeutics to address the growing threat posed by viruses, particularly those that pose significant risks to human health.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This dissertation outlines recent advances in the discovery and development of small-molecule entry inhibitors targeting viruses that encode Class 1 fusion proteins, which are critical for viral entry into host cells.
analysis.methods: The research focuses on identifying and optimizing small-molecule inhibitors that target Class 1 fusion proteins, which are essential for viral entry, and evaluates their effectiveness against specific viruses of concern.
analysis.main_results: The study highlights the development of thieno[3,2-b]pyrroles as novel Group 2 influenza A virus entry inhibitors and further optimizes the raloxifene-inspired benzothiophenes scaffold as novel pan-filovirus entry inhibitors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings introduce new compounds that show promise in inhibiting viral entry, offering potential advancements in antiviral therapy for specific viral targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results could inform the development of targeted antiviral therapies for viruses that encode Class 1 fusion proteins, potentially improving treatment options for viral infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a dissertation and does not provide detailed experimental results or statistical analyses, limiting the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This dissertation addresses the urgent need for novel antiviral therapeutics by focusing on the development of small-molecule entry inhibitors targeting viruses that encode Class 1 fusion proteins. The study highlights recent advances in identifying and optimizing compounds that inhibit viral entry, specifically thieno[3,2-b]pyrroles for Group 2 influenza A virus and raloxifene-inspired benzothiophenes for pan-filovirus. The findings introduce new potential antiviral agents, which could inform future therapeutic strategies for viruses with similar entry mechanisms. However, the study is based on a dissertation and lacks detailed experimental results or statistical analyses, which limits the strength of the evidence. The research contributes to the understanding of antiviral entry inhibition and may have implications for the development of targeted therapies for viral infections.

title: Cytoplasmic ATR orchestrates PRRSV and EBOV replication organelle assembly via vimentin phosphorylation

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of ATR in viral replication, particularly in the context of RNA viruses, and to address the knowledge gap regarding its noncanonical functions beyond the DNA damage response.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the replication of two distinct RNA viruses, PRRSV and EBOV, and examined the role of ATR in their life cycle, specifically during the replication stage.
analysis.methods: The researchers used acute pharmacologic inhibition or knockdown of ATR to assess its impact on viral replication and RO formation, and they demonstrated ATR's direct interaction with and phosphorylation of vimentin within ROs.
analysis.main_results: Acute inhibition or knockdown of ATR significantly suppressed viral replication and reduced the formation of double-membrane vesicles and membrane-less condensates essential for ROs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal a conserved ATR-vimentin signaling axis that promotes RO biogenesis across diverse RNA viruses, highlighting a novel noncanonical function of cytoplasmic ATR in orchestrating replication compartments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the molecular mechanisms of viral replication and may inform the development of antiviral strategies targeting ATR-vimentin interactions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro observations and does not address in vivo relevance, but the evidence is robust and consistent across both PRRSV and EBOV infections.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of ATR in RNA virus replication, revealing a conserved mechanism through which ATR promotes the formation of replication organelles (ROs) by phosphorylating vimentin. The research demonstrates that ATR inhibition or knockdown suppresses viral replication and reduces RO formation in both PRRSV and EBOV. These findings highlight a novel noncanonical function of ATR in orchestrating the assembly of replication compartments, which could inform future antiviral strategies. However, the study is limited to in vitro settings and does not explore in vivo implications. The evidence is strong and consistent across both viral models, suggesting a broad relevance to RNA virus biology.

title: Delayed international support has hampered efforts to contain and treat Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the challenges of containing and treating Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo, highlighting the impact of delayed international support on outbreak management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is based on the author's personal experience during the 2014-16 Ebola epidemic in West Africa and the current outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, focusing on the experiences of families, health workers, and communities affected by the disease.
analysis.methods: The author describes their role as a medical doctor and epidemiologist in the African Union Ebola response mission, detailing the challenges of trust, community engagement, and the importance of timely international support in outbreak control.
analysis.main_results: The 2014-16 epidemic in West Africa caused more than 28,600 cases and 11,300 deaths, and the current outbreak in the DRC has reported 10,305 confirmed cases and 4,996 deaths across five countries as of May 2026.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The author interprets the findings as emphasizing the critical need for timely international support to effectively manage Ebola outbreaks, noting that delayed responses can lead to more severe consequences.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of international collaboration and rapid response mechanisms in preventing the spread of Ebola virus disease and improving outbreak containment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on personal experience and observational data, which may introduce bias and limit the generalizability of the findings. The confidence in the evidence is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This article discusses the challenges of containing and treating Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo, emphasizing the impact of delayed international support. The author draws on their experience during the 2014-16 epidemic in West Africa and the current outbreak in the DRC, highlighting the importance of community trust, timely information, and effective international collaboration. The study reports that the 2014-16 epidemic caused over 28,600 cases and 11,300 deaths, while the current outbreak has already resulted in 10,305 confirmed cases and 4,996 deaths. The author interprets these findings as demonstrating the critical need for timely international support to manage outbreaks effectively. The article underscores the significance of rapid response and community engagement in preventing the spread of Ebola virus disease. However, the evidence is based on personal experience and observational data, which may introduce bias and limit the generalizability of the findings, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.
